paragraphs.text: [PDF page 1] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires Jenifer Rajkumar Candidate's Full Name Jenifer Rajkumar Candidate's Pronouns She/Her Do you identify as a member of the LGBTQ community? If so, please specify as you are comfortable* No. I am a strong ally. Office New York State Assembly District Number 38 Full Name of Campaign Committee(s) Jenifer Rajkumar for New York Campaign Website www.jeniferforny.com Campaign Social Media Handles @JeniferRajkumar for everything If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? If no, please explain. Yes, proudly. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you are seeking? I am a proven legislator and lifelong civil rights advocate. Before the Assembly, I was a workers’ rights attorney and New York State's Director of Immigration Affairs, where I created a first in the nation legal defense project for immigrants. In office, I have passed major legislation, delivered strong constituent services, and fought for working families, immigrants, women, and marginalized communities. I bring history-making results, unrelenting energy, and a deep commitment to justice. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBTQ movement. Please be specific. Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 1

[PDF page 2] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires My commitment to the LGBTQ movement is longstanding, public, and deeply personal. Early in my career, I spoke out against Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell, which targeted gay servicemembers for discrimination. I marched for marriage equality, and I continue to march every year in the Pride Parade. I have also proudly marched in St. Pat’s for All, which represents the values of inclusion and equality that I believe must define public life. In my own district, I defeated an incumbent who voted against marriage equality and GENDA, and I made it a priority to throw open the doors of my office and district to LGBTQ organizations and advocates. I have actively supported LGBTQ groups and worked to ensure they have a real partner in government. As a new Assembly Member, I spoke on the floor in support of repealing the Walking While Trans ban. In those remarks, I highlighted the unjust targeting of the trans community and the violence and hate crimes this community continues to face. I have also spoken out regularly for LGBTQ youth, who deserve safety, affirmation, and the freedom to grow up as their full selves. This session, I am supporting funding for gender affirming care in the state budget. And as the first South Asian woman ever elected to a New York State office, I feel a special responsibility to open safe and inclusive spaces for South Asian LGBTQ people, who too often face invisibility or isolation. This work is very important to me, and I see it as part of my duty as a civil rights leader and public servant. What are your policy priorities if you are to win this seat? How will these policy priorities impact the LGBTQ community? My policy priorities are affordability, healthcare, civil rights, public safety, and honest government that truly works for people. I believe government must open the doors of opportunity for every New Yorker, and those priorities have direct importance for the LGBTQ community. First, I will continue fighting for affordability and economic security. Too many New Yorkers are being crushed by the cost of housing, healthcare, groceries, and everyday life. LGBTQ New Yorkers, especially LGBTQ youth, transgender New Yorkers, LGBTQ seniors, and LGBTQ people of color, are disproportionately vulnerable to poverty, housing instability, family rejection, and economic insecurity. That means affordability is not separate from LGBTQ equality. Expanding affordable housing, protecting tenants, creating pathways to good jobs, defending workers’ rights, and strengthening the safety net are all essential to helping LGBTQ New Yorkers live with dignity and stability. Second, I will continue making healthcare a major priority. Healthcare must include not only affordable insurance and treatment, but access to respectful, culturally competent care. I support protecting and expanding access to gender affirming care, mental health care, preventive care, and HIV prevention and treatment. For many LGBTQ New Yorkers, especially trans New Yorkers and young people, access to affirming healthcare can be life changing and even lifesaving. I want New York to remain a place where people can get the care they need without stigma, fear, or political interference. Third, I will continue advancing civil rights and anti-discrimination protections. The LGBTQ community must be able to live openly and safely, free from discrimination in employment, housing, education, healthcare, and public accommodations. I will oppose any effort to roll back equality or target LGBTQ people for exclusion. I have always believed that discrimination anywhere diminishes justice everywhere, and I will continue to use my office to protect equal Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 2

[PDF page 3] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires dignity under law. Public safety is also an LGBTQ issue. Safety means freedom from hate crimes, harassment, violence, and bias. It means making sure trans New Yorkers are not profiled, targeted, or treated as less worthy of protection. It means ensuring LGBTQ youth are safe in schools and communities. I will continue speaking out against hate, supporting strong protections for vulnerable communities, and working for a New York where every person can walk down the street safely as themselves. I also believe deeply in the importance of representation and inclusion. As the first South Asian woman ever elected to a New York State office, I feel a special responsibility to make government more inclusive and to open safe spaces for people who have too often been unseen, including South Asian LGBTQ New Yorkers. There are many people living at the intersection of multiple identities who deserve to know that their government sees them, values them, and will fight for them. Finally, I will continue my commitment to good government, because corruption, indifference, and inaction always hurt marginalized communities first and worst. LGBTQ New Yorkers deserve leaders who do not just speak the language of equality, but actually deliver results. My goal is to build a government that is accessible, compassionate, and courageous enough to defend people’s rights in moments when it matters most. When re-elected, I will continue fighting for a New York where LGBTQ people can live safely, openly, affordably, and with full opportunity. That is not a side issue to me. It is central to the kind of just society I believe government must build. Please list here the union, organizations (community, civic, media, issue groups), LGBTQ leaders, and elected officials that have endorsed you. 32BJ, HTC, IBEW Local 3, NY State Troopers, U.S. Congressmember Gregory Meeks; Speaker Carl Heastie; SENATORS John Liu, James Sanders, Joe Addabbo; ASSEMBLY MEMBERS Andrew Hevesi, Chuck Lavine, Kalman Yeger, Sam Berger, Nily Rozic, Steve Stern, Rodneyse Bichotte, Stacey Pheffer Amato, George Alvarez; COUNCILMEMBERS Lynn Schulman, Oswald Feliz, Phil Wong, Bob Holden Have you ever endorsed any LGBTQ candidates? Which ones? Councilmember Lynn Schulman, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin Would you in the future endorse, appoint or financially support any candidate for public office, elected official, or political appointee with a record of opposing LGBTQ equality? If yes, please explain. * No. It is unconscionable to deny the humanity of an entire community. Across the nation, and in New York State, we have seen a massive wave of anti LGBTQ legislation, including restricting the rights of trans youth, bans on LGBTQ books in schools, limits on drag queen performances, and limits on gender affirming care for minors and adults. How would you use your platform as a New York State Legislator to advocate for the protection of LGBTQ people across the city, state, and country? We are living through a coordinated and dangerous wave of anti LGBTQ attacks across the country, and this is not a moment for caution or quiet concern. It is a moment to fight back. As a New York State Legislator, I use my platform not Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 3

[PDF page 4] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires only to defend the LGBTQ community, but to go on offense for equality, dignity, safety, and freedom. This is an opportunity to make New York a national leader. We should not merely hold the line while other states move backward. We should expand protections and show the country what moral leadership looks like. In the State Assembly and in the budget, I support initiatives that protect access to gender affirming care, strengthen mental health care, defend LGBTQ youth, and ensure schools and public institutions remain safe and inclusive. This session, I support funding for gender affirming care. It is a human right and, for many people, lifesaving care. I also support strong funding for mental health services, including my Empire State of Mind Act, which revamps our mental health system by closing gaps and creating a true continuum of care. That matters especially for vulnerable youth, including LGBTQ youth, who too often face bullying, rejection, trauma, and isolation. I believe elected officials must be vocal, visible, and unwavering when any community is under attack. I use every part of this office-- legislation, budget advocacy, public speaking, coalition building, media, and direct partnership with community organizations--to make clear that New York will not be dragged backward by hatred and fear. When extremists target trans youth, censor books, attack drag performers, or try to strip away gender affirming care, we must answer with action. I also use my platform to defend LGBTQ students and families from censorship and erasure. Book bans and attacks on inclusive education are not about protecting children. They are about teaching fear, shame, and silence. I continue speaking out against those efforts and in favor of schools where every child can see themselves reflected, respected, and safe. I have shown that I do not sit on the sidelines. In my own district, I defeated an incumbent who voted against marriage equality and GENDA, and I opened the doors of my district to LGBTQ organizations. Early in my career, I spoke out against Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell. I marched for marriage equality. I march every year in the Pride Parade and in St. Pat’s for All. As a new Assembly Member, I spoke on the floor for repeal of the Walking While Trans ban, highlighting the targeting of the trans community and the hate crimes this community continues to face. I speak out regularly for LGBTQ youth, because they deserve affirmation, protection, and hope. I continue using my office to help make New York a refuge. That means protecting patients, supporting providers, standing with LGBTQ organizations, and using my public voice to challenge hateful rhetoric wherever it appears. It also means recognizing that attacks on LGBTQ people are tied to broader attacks on bodily autonomy, free expression, public education, and civil rights. We must meet that challenge with solidarity and courage. As the first South Asian woman ever elected to New York State office, I also feel a special responsibility to create safe, inclusive spaces for those who have too often been unseen, including South Asian LGBTQ people. I work to open doors and opportunity for them, and to make sure they know they belong fully in public life and in our movement for justice. At this moment, New York cannot be timid. We must lead. I am proud to be part of that fight. The LGBTQ community has historically been overpoliced, and research shows that law enforcement continues to disproportionately target marginalized people: What do you view as the New York State Legislature's role in ensuring law enforcement oversight, funding, and role in meeting the needs of marginalized communities? What, if any, relevant policy proposals do you support regarding law enforcement? Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 4

[PDF page 5] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires The State Legislature has a critical role in ensuring that public safety is rooted in justice, accountability, and equal protection under law. For too long, the LGBTQ community, especially transgender people, LGBTQ youth, homeless youth, sex workers, and LGBTQ people of color, has been overpoliced, profiled, and treated as suspect rather than protected. That history cannot be ignored, and it must not be repeated. The Legislature must set the legal and budgetary framework to ensure that law enforcement is accountable to the public and responsive to the needs of marginalized communities. That includes strengthening oversight, increasing transparency, supporting data collection on bias and hate crimes, and ensuring consequences for misconduct. Public dollars should never flow without public accountability. I strongly supported repeal of the Walking While Trans ban because it was a clear example of how the law was used to target and criminalize trans New Yorkers, especially trans women of color. When I spoke on the floor in support of repeal, I highlighted the unjust targeting of the trans community and the violence and hate crimes this community continues to face. I also believe police are not the answer to every social problem. Mental health crises, homelessness, substance use, and youth vulnerability often require care, treatment, and trained professionals rather than only enforcement. That is why I authored the 20 page Empire State of Mind Act, the most comprehensive mental health bill in 60 years, to revamp our mental health system by closing the gaps and creating a true continuum of care. We need prevention, crisis response, treatment, supportive housing, and long term follow up, so people do not fall through the cracks until they end up in crisis. Real public safety means marginalized communities are protected from violence and hate, but not subjected to biased enforcement themselves. That is what I will keep fighting for. New York State is experiencing a housing crisis, and the LGBTQ community disproportionately experiences homelessness, especially our LGBTQ youth and seniors. How do you intend to ensure that any housing plan is equitable to the LGBTQ Community and other marginalized groups? The LGBTQ community, especially LGBTQ youth and seniors, faces disproportionate rates of homelessness, housing insecurity, family rejection, and discrimination. That means equity must be built into housing policy from the beginning. I support increasing the supply of deeply affordable housing, not just market-rate development with small affordable set-asides. We need stronger tenant protections, eviction prevention, rental assistance, anti-harassment enforcement, and measures to prevent displacement in vulnerable communities. I also support expanding supportive housing and transitional housing, especially for people facing the greatest barriers to stability. For LGBTQ youth, that means funding safe, affirming emergency shelter beds, transitional housing, and long-term supportive housing for young people who have been rejected by their families or forced into homelessness. For LGBTQ seniors, it means creating and preserving affordable housing where they can age with dignity, security, and freedom from discrimination or isolation, with access to supportive services when needed. We also need clear standards and oversight to ensure shelters, supportive housing, and transitional housing providers are affirming and culturally competent. No one should be denied housing, mistreated, misgendered, or made unsafe Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 5

[PDF page 6] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires because of who they are. That is especially important for transgender New Yorkers, who too often face bias even within systems meant to provide help. I also believe housing policy must connect to the larger conditions that create instability in the first place. That means protecting workers, expanding access to benefits, supporting mental health care, and enforcing fair housing and anti-discrimination laws. If someone has formal legal equality but cannot find a safe place to live, then equality is incomplete. I will continue fighting for housing policy that names the needs of LGBTQ New Yorkers and meets them with real protections, targeted resources, and lasting opportunity. In today’s political climate, what role should the New York Legislature play in protecting and expanding access to comprehensive reproductive and gender-affirming healthcare? Will you commit to defending access to abortion care and gender-affirming care for both adults and youth, including taking legislative action to prevent hospitals and healthcare systems—such as NYU Langone Health—from restricting or ending lifesaving care due to political pressure or federal intimidation? * The New York Legislature must play a leading role in protecting and expanding access to comprehensive reproductive and gender affirming healthcare. In this political climate, these rights cannot be treated as settled. They must be actively defended. Yes, I absolutely commit to defending access to abortion care and gender affirming care for both adults and youth. This work is deeply personal to me. I previously worked in the Reproductive Justice Division of the National Women’s Law Center, and I have been active in the reproductive justice movement for years. Equality and bias free medicine are especially important to me because I come from a family of doctors. I grew up with a deep respect for medicine as a calling and for the principle that healthcare must serve patients with dignity, fairness, and compassion. Bodily autonomy is a core freedom. The right to make decisions about your own body, your own healthcare, and your own future is fundamental to equal citizenship. That includes abortion care, contraception, fertility care, and gender affirming care. When politicians or institutions interfere in those deeply personal decisions, they are taking away freedom. New York must not back down in the face of political pressure or federal intimidation. I support legislative action to ensure that hospitals and healthcare systems cannot restrict, delay, or end medically necessary, lifesaving care because of fear, ideology, or outside pressure. If institutions that serve New Yorkers are retreating from essential care, then the Legislature has a duty to act. This session, I support funding for gender affirming care in the state budget because it is healthcare, and often lifesaving healthcare. I also support strengthening protections for providers and patients, safeguarding access to abortion, and making clear that New York will remain a refuge for those seeking care. That includes young people, who are too often the first targets of cruel political attacks. Trans youth deserve support, safety, and healthcare, not scapegoating. At a moment when others are retreating from freedom, New York must lead with courage. I am committed to being a strong voice in that fight. Privacy Amendment S8603 (Ramos) / A9377 (Shimsky) This amendment would enshrine a fundamental right to privacy in the New York Constitution, protecting personal decisions, bodily autonomy, and limiting government Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 6

It is especially critical for LGBTQ+ New Yorkers whose sensitive data could otherwise be misused or weaponized. Yes Comprehensive Sex Education (CSE) S6901A (Salazar) / A7496 (Gonzalez-Rojas) This bill ensures age-appropriate, inclusive sex education statewide that reflects national standards. It reduces stigma, affirms LGBTQ+ students, and promotes safer, more informed school environments. Yes New York for All Act S2235 (Gounardes) / A3506 (Reyes) This bill limits state and local involvement in immigration enforcement, protecting immigrant families and public safety. It is vital for safeguarding LGBTQ+ immigrants who face heightened risks of targeting and discrimination. Yes Holding Police Accountable by Strengthening the Civilian Complaint Review Board S4354 (Bailey) / A126 (Cruz) This act expands the CCRB’s authority to investigate bias-based policing, which disproportionately harms LGBTQ+ people, particularly LGBTQ+ New Yorkers of color. It is a necessary step toward real accountability and trust in law enforcement. Yes The Gender Identity Respect Dignity and Safety Act (GIRDS) (A5478A - Gallagher/ S1049A Salazar) This bill ensures incarcerated transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals are treated with dignity, respected in placement, and provided gender-affirming necessities. It significantly improves safety and reduces abuse in correctional settings. Yes A6059 (Simone) / S03227 (Hoylman - Sigal) Prohibits health insurers, health care plans and HMOs from requiring prior authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis used to prevent HIV infection Yes The Freedom to Read Act S8630 (May) / A9537 (Simone) This bill prevents book bans based on LGBTQ+ identity or family structure in schools and libraries. It protects intellectual freedom and ensures young people can access accurate, inclusive representations of themselves and others.
